brief.headline: We project the 2026/27 US crop at 12.69m bales (all cotton; upland 12.31m), 0.48m below the November 2026 WASDE (13.18m). Texas drives the gap: 2.92m vs USDA 4.10m, on 52% projected abandonment.
points: BMR-Com crop projection (2026-11-27): US upland 12.31m bales (95% 10.3–14.7m; 99% 9.7–15.6m) vs USDA 12.79m; all cotton 12.69m vs WASDE 13.18m. Texas 2.92m (95% 2.2–3.9m) vs USDA 4.10m, with final Texas abandonment projected at 52% (95% 34–69%) against 34% in USDA's numbers.

Conditional view (Texas built as harvested acres × yield): abandonment 47% of 5.9m planted leaves 3.12m harvested acres (95% 2.05–3.85m); at USDA's 505 lb (95% 414–618) Texas is 3.28m (95% 2.07–4.21m). US upland 12.67m (95% 10.83–14.11m), all cotton 13.05m. Past seasons with similar Texas ratings ended at 42–75% abandonment.

Texas FSA failed acres (November release) are 14.7% of planted. Failed acres are reported to FSA with a lag and the December–January releases settle them, so the abandonment projection uses this season's drought and ratings readings against what similar readings meant for final abandonment in past seasons.
Classing by office to Nov 20: South Texas (Corpus Christi) 1,226k bales classed; West Texas (Lubbock 341k, Lamesa 95k, Abilene 120k) 557k. West Texas classing is now well under way.

Cross-check — Drought model: Texas abandonment 48.7% (±14 pts) from the highest-R² drought model (D1-D4 cumulative, R² 58%, cotton-area drought through 2026-10-27), against 33.9% implied by USDA, at USDA's 505 lb yield: Texas 3.18m bales, US crop 12.26m (±1σ 11.41–13.11m).

Cross-check — Ratings model: Texas condition index 2.49 (latest two weeks) points to 311 lb per planted acre (USDA 334; fit R² 0.82 over 2001–2025): Texas 3.82m bales, US crop 12.90m (±1σ 12.37–13.52m).
Cross-check — Average of the two, Texas 3.50m (USDA 4.10m), US crop 12.58m (±1σ 12.05–13.22m); every other state at USDA's latest.

Balance sheet (WASDE 2026/27, our crop): beginning stocks 4.15m + crop 12.58m + imports 0.01m − mill use 1.40m − exports 12.30m = ending stocks 3.11m (stocks/use 22.7% vs WASDE 27.0%); ±1σ 2.58–3.75m. These stocks drive the price and spread fair values on the model tabs.

Crop-progress cross-check (ratings, drought, FSA failed acres, classing): US upland 12.25m vs USDA 12.79m (-4.2%). It is higher than the drought model because it projects Texas abandonment lower; it would replace the headline only if it proves the better predictor.
Crop ratings: 33% good/excellent and 37% poor/very poor nationally.

Texas abandonment: FSA failed acres are 14.7% of reported plantings so far, but failed acres keep rising after October — on this season's drought and ratings we project final abandonment of 39% (state average 36%), vs 34% implied by USDA. Yield 495 lb vs USDA 505; 5% of Texas in D2–D4 drought.
Largest gaps to USDA: Arkansas 1.04m vs 1.60m; Texas 3.72m vs 4.10m; Oklahoma 0.38m vs 0.20m.
Harvest 84% complete vs 79% last year and 83% on average.
NASS ginnings to Mid Nov (Nov 15, 2026): 5.70m running bales, 42.1% of last season's total (normal 45.9% by this date).

Projection from ginnings: 12.14m bales (±1σ 11.57m–12.73m), -5.1% vs USDA, with 56% of it resting on ginning so far; Texas ginning pace alone points to 3.13m (415 lb on harvested acres after projected abandonment).
6.75m upland bales classed this season through Nov 26, -11% vs the same week last year; normally 52% of the crop is classed by now.

Quality so far: tenderable 82.0% (+0.0 pts vs last year); color 31 & better 55.9% (+7.6 pts vs last year); staple 36.43 (-0.35 vs last year); mike 5.0+ discount 7.6% (-3.6 pts vs last year); strength 30.8 g/tex (-0.3 vs last year).
